decision_brief.lede: The six files in this folder show no supported security problem. The program reads one optional config file, sends only the city name to Open-Meteo, and has no install scripts. This is a scoped static result, not a guarantee the tool is safe.
decision_brief.summary_title: No findings in the reviewed files
summary: src/cli.js reads only ~/.config/weather-cli/config.json (the city field) and queries two fixed Open-Meteo HTTPS endpoints; the city is URL-encoded.
package.json has no preinstall, install, postinstall or prepare scripts, and the single dependency kleur 4.1.5 is pinned with an integrity hash.
The README statement about what is sent matches the code.
result_meaning: No finding was supported by a reachable path within these six files.
The kleur package source was not read, so this does not cover third-party code, and nothing was run.

surface_review.summary: README.md is short and factual; no credential requests, urgency, fake identity or instructions to disable safeguards. It labels itself a synthetic fixture.
Only ~/.config/weather-cli/config.json is read, and only its city value is used; no env vars, keys, browser profiles or other home files are referenced.

Two fixed destinations (geocoding-api.open-meteo.com, api.open-meteo.com). Sent data: the encoded city name, then coordinates returned by the first API. No encoding, redirects to other hosts or other sinks.
No MCP config, agent files, skills, hooks, editor tasks or CI workflows in the folder.
No lifecycle scripts or downloads. The only script is test: node --test, run only if invoked. The README suggests npx weather-cli.
One dependency, kleur 4.1.5, exact-pinned in package.json and lockfile (lockfileVersion 3) with registry.npmjs.org URL and sha512 integrity. Package contents not inspected.

rejected_candidates.title: Config file read followed by network requests (possible data exfiltration)
rejected_candidates.reason: Only the city string from the config reaches the network, as documented in the README; destinations are fixed constants. A config with extra fields does not send them. A non-string city is stringified by encodeURIComponent and sent only to Open-Meteo.

rejected_candidates.title: Unvalidated JSON.parse of user config and API responses
rejected_candidates.reason: The config is the user's own file; a malformed file or response only crashes the CLI. No injection sink, no eval, no shell, no file writes.

rejected_candidates.title: bin entry plus npx usage executes code on run
rejected_candidates.reason: Running a CLI is its stated purpose and the code was reviewed; there is no install-time execution.

summary: The project .npmrc sets min-release-age=14, matching the standard 14-day recommendation, and package.json declares packageManager npm@11.10.0, the release that added the key.
Enforcement was not tested: nothing was run, and the npm version actually used on a given machine or in CI, plus user/global config precedence, are unknown.

A cooldown can delay an urgent security fix (npm audit fix may keep a vulnerable version), and older releases are not thereby safe. The lockfile pins kleur 4.1.5; its publication date was not checked.

assessments.limits: Not behavior-tested; a before setting in the same source would take precedence; the packageManager field is only a hint unless Corepack enforces it; min-release-age-exclude was not present; Git, file or tarball sources and user/global config were not assessed. npm docs (v11 config) confirm the unit is days and that npm errors when no version qualifies.

next_steps.text: If you run it, compare the folder against the recorded digest first, and be aware it makes two HTTPS requests to open-meteo.com containing your configured city.
